I know "what distro to use" is an age-old question, but times also change dramatically. I've been a faithful user of Ubuntu since around 11.10 but recently, I've noticed a distinct lack in developer support. You painstakingly post a bug or subscribe to it, but even after ages, its unfixed. In many cases, lots of bugs are even closed as Won't Fix.

I'd like to know how is the openSUSE developer support compared to Ubuntu? Is it better or worse? I've finally decided that trivial things like Desktop Environment (GNOME, KDE, etc.), packaging system (apt vs yum), raw performance, etc. don't matter in the long run. What matters is how is the developer support.

Distro devs are not responsible for upstream bugs, only their own bugs.

So you won't get much help whereever you go if you're asking the wrong people. Of course ubuntu is wilfully different with stuff like unity, mir... bugs there are their business.

I'd think about Debian, or Fedora, before opensuse, unless german was my first language.
I always recommend fedora. (the new mint is apparently very nice as well)

Don't forget to think outside the box. Linux is not constraint to only one install on a PC. You can install different version on different external hard disks each for a specific purpose. You can swap between them by plugging a different USB hard drive. This separates your Linux version, one for games, one for normal operation, one for work and one for porn.

You could also do this with Virtual machines.

And the really cool thing is that if you install all your Linux version in a VM, Then you can use that same VM in Windows and Booted up as a neutral Linux just to boot up the VMWare.
Mint or devuan. Depending on your level of skill. Those two are both terrible choices.

I would say arch is the best as far as community. Their wiki is beast and likely already has any advisal support you need prewritten. As for bugs any fix can get posted to the aur if upstream is being slow, and the bug fix will be shared by all.

If you want help from a bug on another distro what you are really asking for is a workaround to simply move past the bug. That's where that wiki is probably better than any human you'll talk to. These aren't howto's like ubuntu's howto. These are guides for every option with workarounds for running the software on any system. If there is a reconfiguration that can help you get past a bug in the immediate the config option will be listed there.

If a config option won't fix it and it's just plain broken, there's not much ubuntu or suse would do for you. If it's broken it's broken. They can't reach into your computer and flip the bits to make it magically correct code.
